digest.component_or_area: tickets store fetch and initialization in CI
propositions: A full clone of the tickets store costs 1.04 GiB / 59s wall time; partial clone with blob:none filter reduces this to 68.7 MiB / 14.3s (~15x reduction) while preserving the complete commit graph needed for merge-base and ancestry scoping.

When a tickets fetch times out in CI, rebar silently bootstraps a fresh orphan store via worktree add --orphan, diverging from origin/tickets and causing all reads to return empty and writes to land on an unreachable branch.

Blobless partial clones are safe for rebar's access patterns: verify-identity scans work on tree-level diffs with event/keyring bodies read from the working tree, and no lazy-fetch storms occur in advisory mode.

The reconcile-bridge workflow must set merge.ours.driver=true before applying blob:none filters, otherwise git silently degrades .bridge_state merge conflicts to a broken 3-way text merge of an 18 MB JSON file.

The gerrit-verify.yaml verify-identity job performs a full 51,575-commit clone (6.73m wall time, 92% of job duration) where a blob:none partial clone with era-scoping via merge-base would achieve 6x speedup without compromising commit-ancestry requirements.

git blame over historical trees required for derive_caused_by must either fail closed (returning None and preventing partial/incorrect caused_by links) or abort rather than silently elect a culprit from incomplete path data.
